title: Workspace Privacy Lens — access paths visualizer and remediation cards
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Design a compact, queryable 'Workspace Privacy Lens' view in the Redwood Console that surfaces how access is granted to a selected workspace resource (API key, model route, dashboard) across direct grants, role inheritance, cross-workspace shares, and temporary delegations. The view should combine an interactive graph of access paths, a timeline scrubber for historical changes, and a stack of contextual remediation cards that let admins preview the effect of changes before applying them.
goals: Make it easy to answer: who can act as X on this resource, and how did those permissions change over time
Provide lightweight remediation suggestions (revoke, narrow scope, convert to role) with an estimated user- and cost-impact preview
Support audit and compliance workflows: exportable snapshots, annotations, and links to related incident tickets
Fit into Console rollouts and canary checks by surfacing risky changes before they are promoted
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a workspace resource opens the Privacy Lens panel with an access-path graph and timeline scrubber
Graph nodes show principal type (user, service, role, external) and hover reveals grant metadata (grantor, created_at, origin - API/Console/Provisioning)
Timeline scrubber lets reviewers step through changes and shows diff highlights for permissions added/removed
Remediation cards propose concrete actions with a preview: affected principals list, downstream implications, and cost delta estimation
Snapshots can be exported as JSON/CSV and linked to a Linear ticket template
Prototype usability test with 6 PM/Platform engineers achieves median success time under 3 minutes for 'identify all principals with write' scenario
tasks: Finalize information hierarchy for graph nodes and card compact view
Design micro-interactions for timeline scrubber and play/pause history replay
Create two density variants: compact list and expanded graph for power users
Define copy for remediation actions and confirmation modals (safety-first language)
Coordinate with frontend on data model: required fields and pagination contract
Prepare usability test script and recruit participants from Platform and Security teams
decisions: Prefer deterministic, non-animated graph layout for initial release to avoid distracting admins
Include cost-delta estimate only for changes that affect token-serving routes; show 'not applicable' for other resources
Remediation flows are advisory by default; destructive actions require escalation to the owner (per existing policy)
review_comments: Maren: prefer showing 'last verified' timestamp next to principal to support audits
Leila: add exportable evidence bundle (audit snapshot + signed metadata) for compliance requests
Carlos: backend will only provide full history for 12 months initially — design should show ellipses and 'older history truncated' hint
notes: Prototype emphasizes quick triage for on-call and platform teams. We deliberately avoid in-panel role editing in v1 to reduce blast radius; remediation cards open a small guided workflow handled by a separate ticket. Pairing session with ENG scheduled 2026-03-12 to reconcile data availability and telemetry hooks. Consider later linking cost-breakdown per principal for Dedicated customers.
